questions.subject: dev
questions.title: True statement about the primitive streak
questions.question: Primitive streak:

options.A: Appears at the cranial end of the embryonic disc
options.B: Its formation indicates the beginning of gastrulation
options.D: Appears at the end of the 3rd week
options.E: Forms the primitive node at its caudal end

explanations.A: Incorrect. The primitive streak appears in the caudal part of the embryonic disc, not the cranial end.
explanations.B: Correct. The primitive streak is a median thickening formed by proliferation and migration of epiblast cells. Its appearance is the first visible sign of gastrulation, the process that converts the bilaminar disc into a trilaminar one. By convention, the streak's own formation is therefore taken to mark the beginning of gastrulation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The primitive streak is formed by epiblast cells, not hypoblast cells; the hypoblast is instead displaced by the epiblast-derived endoderm during gastrulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The primitive streak appears at the beginning of the third week, not its end.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The primitive streak forms the primitive node at its cranial end, not its caudal end; the node is the rounded bulge at the streak's cranial-most point, with the primitive pit in its middle.

questions.learning_objective: State that the primitive streak's formation marks the beginning of gastrulation.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.18/p.19 row 69 (b, remark explicitly spells out why d and e are wrong: "(d) is wrong because it appears at beginning of 3rd week. (e) is wrong because it forms the primitive node at its cranial end."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.10-11

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Structures the neurenteric canal temporarily connects
questions.question: Neurenteric canal is a temporary connection between:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The extraembryonic coelom is not one of the two cavities the neurenteric canal connects.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The extraembryonic coelom is not one of the two cavities the neurenteric canal connects.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The neural tube is not a cavity the neurenteric canal connects to at all.
explanations.D: Correct. The primitive pit, a small depression in the primitive node, deepens and extends ventrally. It briefly connects the amniotic cavity above the embryonic disc with the yolk sac cavity below it, and this transient passage is the neurenteric canal. It normally closes again as the notochordal process solidifies.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The intraembryonic coelom is not one of the two cavities the neurenteric canal connects.

questions.learning_objective: State that the neurenteric canal is a temporary connection between the amniotic cavity and the yolk sac.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Origin of the visceral pericardium
questions.question: Visceral pericardium originates from:

options.A: Splanchnic layer of lateral plate mesoderm
options.B: Somatic layer of lateral plate mesoderm

explanations.A: Correct. Lateral plate mesoderm splits into a somatic (parietal) layer, applied to the ectoderm, and a splanchnic (visceral) layer, applied to the endoderm of the gut tube. The splanchnic layer gives the visceral layer of every serous membrane inside the body cavity, including the visceral pericardium around the heart, the visceral pleura around the lungs and the visceral peritoneum around the abdominal viscera.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The somatic layer of lateral plate mesoderm forms the parietal layers of the serous membranes and the connective tissue of the body wall and limbs, not the visceral pericardium.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Paraxial mesoderm forms the somites (axial skeleton, dermis and skeletal muscle), not the serous membranes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Intermediate mesoderm forms the urogenital system, not the serous membranes.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The intraembryonic splanchnic layer, not the extraembryonic mesoderm, gives the visceral pericardium; extraembryonic mesoderm instead contributes to the placental membranes.

questions.learning_objective: State that the visceral pericardium originates from the splanchnic layer of lateral plate mesoderm.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Derivative of the neural tube
questions.question: Which one of the following is a derivative of the neural tube?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The autonomic (sympathetic and parasympathetic) nervous system is a neural crest derivative, not a neural tube one.
explanations.B: Correct. The neural folds meet and fuse, beginning in the cervical region and closing towards both ends, to give the neural tube. The neural tube becomes the whole central nervous system, grey and white matter alike. The spinal cord, together with the brain, is therefore a genuine neural tube derivative, unlike the neural-crest or mesodermal options listed alongside it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The suprarenal medulla is a neural crest derivative, not a neural tube one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pia mater is a mesodermal derivative, not a neural tube one.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Schwann cells are neural crest derivatives, not neural tube ones.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Incorrect statement about the primitive node
questions.question: As regards the primitive node, choose the INCORRECT statement:

options.C: It is formed of ectoderm & endoderm
options.D: It has a small pit in its middle
options.E: It is formed at the cephalic end of the primitive streak

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this statement IS true). The primitive node appears during the third gestational week, alongside the primitive streak of which it is a part.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this statement IS true). Cells ingressing through the primitive pit in the node's middle form the prenotochordal process, the first step of notochord formation.
explanations.C: Correct. This is the false statement, the one the question asks for. The primitive node is a rounded proliferation of epiblast cells at the cranial end of the primitive streak, not a structure formed of ectoderm and endoderm; it is the primitive (bucco-pharyngeal) and cloacal membranes, not the primitive node, that are formed of directly fused ectoderm and endoderm.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this statement IS true). The primitive node has the primitive pit, a small depression, in its middle.
explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. this statement IS true). The primitive node is formed at the cephalic (cranial) end of the primitive streak.

questions.learning_objective: Identify that the primitive node is formed of proliferating epiblast cells, not of fused ectoderm and endoderm.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Site where ectoderm and endoderm meet at the caudal end of the primitive streak
questions.question: At caudal end of the primitive streak, ectoderm & endoderm meet at:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The notochordal canal is a transient cavity within the developing notochord, not a site of ectoderm-endoderm fusion.
explanations.B: Correct. At the caudal end of the primitive streak, ectoderm and endoderm are directly fused with no intervening mesoderm. This fusion forms the cloacal membrane, the future site of the anal and urogenital openings. It is one of the two membranous absence sites this question cluster tests repeatedly, the other being the oropharyngeal membrane at the streak's cranial end.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The buccopharyngeal (oropharyngeal) membrane is the equivalent fusion site at the cranial, not caudal, end, just beyond the primitive node.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The intraembryonic coelom is a fluid-filled space within the lateral plate mesoderm, not a site of ectoderm-endoderm fusion.
explanations.E: Incorrect, since option B correctly names the cloacal membrane.

questions.learning_objective: State that ectoderm and endoderm meet directly at the cloacal membrane, at the caudal end of the primitive streak.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.19 row 74 (b, remark: "Cloacal membrane."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.11 and p.19

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Week the intraembryonic mesoderm develops
questions.question: The intraembryonic mesoderm develops in:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The first week is occupied by fertilisation, cleavage and early blastocyst formation, well before any mesoderm exists.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The second week is occupied by implantation and formation of the bilaminar disc (epiblast and hypoblast only), before mesoderm appears.
explanations.C: Correct. Intraembryonic mesoderm arises during gastrulation, the characteristic event of the third week. Epiblast cells ingress through the primitive streak and spread between the epiblast-derived ectoderm and endoderm to form this new middle layer. This third-week timing is the same fact Q44 and Q5 both draw on elsewhere in this bank.
explanations.D: Incorrect. By the fourth week, folding is underway and the three germ layers, mesoderm included, are already established.
explanations.E: Incorrect. By the eighth week, organogenesis is well advanced, far later than mesoderm's initial appearance.

questions.learning_objective: State that intraembryonic mesoderm develops during the third week, as part of gastrulation.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.19 row 75 (c, remark: "Intraembryonic mesoderm develops in 3rd week."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.11 and p.19

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Site the neural crest appears along
questions.question: The neural crest appears along the prominent margins of:

explanations.A: Correct. As the neural folds, the raised lips of the neural groove, meet and fuse to form the neural tube, cells at their crests separate off as a distinct population. This population, the neural crest, then migrates throughout the embryo to form a wide range of peripheral structures. The neural crest therefore arises specifically along the prominent margins of the neural folds, at the point where the folds' edges meet.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The notochord lies beneath the neural plate and induces it, but the neural crest does not arise along the notochord itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The neurenteric canal is an unrelated transient connection between the amniotic cavity and yolk sac, not the site of neural crest formation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The anterior neuropore is the cranial opening of the still-unfused neural tube; the neural crest arises from the folds' margins generally, not specifically at this opening.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The posterior neuropore is likewise a transient opening of the unfused neural tube, not the specific site of neural crest formation.

questions.learning_objective: State that the neural crest arises along the prominent margins of the neural folds as they fuse.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.19 row 76 (a, remark: "Neural crest appears along margins of neural folds."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.11 and p.19

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Structure derived from endoderm
questions.question: Which of the following is derived from endoderm?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The spleen develops from mesenchyme (mesoderm) within the dorsal mesogastrium, not from endoderm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The kidneys develop from intermediate mesoderm, not endoderm.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Blood vessels develop from mesoderm, not endoderm.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lymphatics, like blood vessels, develop from mesoderm, not endoderm.
explanations.E: Correct. The respiratory system arises as an endodermal outgrowth of the foregut, the laryngotracheal diverticulum. The epithelium lining the airway down to the alveoli is therefore endodermal, the same germ layer that lines the rest of the gut tube. The surrounding cartilage, smooth muscle and connective tissue are mesodermal, but the lining epithelium itself is endodermal.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: False statement about the results of folding
questions.question: All the following are results of folding EXCEPT:

options.A: Forebrain is at cranial end of embryo
options.B: Hindgut is enclosed within the tail fold
options.C: Foregut is enclosed within the head fold

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this IS a result of folding). Growth of the neural tube produces a forebrain bulge that comes to lie at the cranial end of the folded embryo.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this IS a result of folding). Tail (caudal) folding encloses the caudal part of the gut tube as the hindgut.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this IS a result of folding). Head (cranial) folding encloses the cranial part of the gut tube as the foregut.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the false statement, the one the question asks for. Folding reverses the connecting stalk's position from caudal to cranial and ventral, not dorsal; it is the disc's flat, dorsally-facing surface that becomes the outer body surface, while the connecting stalk, allantois and body stalk structures are drawn to the ventral aspect.
explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. this IS a result of folding). As the head fold proceeds, the oral (bucco-pharyngeal) membrane is carried to the ventral surface at the floor of the stomodeum.

questions.learning_objective: State that folding brings the connecting stalk to a cranial, ventral position rather than a dorsal one.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.19 row 78 (d, remark: "Connecting stalk becomes ventral."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.11 and p.19

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: False statement about the somites
questions.question: As regards the somites, all the following statements are true EXCEPT:

options.A: They develop from lateral plate mesoderm
options.D: Its dermatomes form dermis of skin

explanations.A: Correct. This is the false statement, the one the question asks for. Somites develop from paraxial mesoderm, not lateral plate mesoderm; paraxial and lateral plate are two separate columns of intraembryonic mesoderm, with the intermediate mesoderm lying between them.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). Each somite's ventromedial part forms the sclerotome.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). Each somite's dorsolateral part forms the dermomyotome, which further splits into a dermatome and a myotome.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). The dermatome portion of the dermomyotome forms the dermis of the skin over most of the body.
explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). The sclerotome portion migrates to surround the notochord and neural tube and forms the vertebral column.

questions.learning_objective: State that somites develop from paraxial mesoderm, not lateral plate mesoderm.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.19 row 79 (a, remark: "Somites develop from paraxial mesoderm."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.12 and p.19

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Mesoderm subdivision showing segmentation
questions.question: Segmentation is observed in the .... mesoderm:

explanations.A: Correct. Paraxial mesoderm is the only intraembryonic mesoderm column that segments. It splits into paired blocks called somitomeres cranially and somites more caudally. This segmental organisation is what later produces the metameric (segmented) pattern of the vertebral column, spinal nerves and associated musculature.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Intermediate mesoderm forms a continuous nephrogenic cord rather than segmenting.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lateral plate mesoderm remains unsegmented, splitting instead into somatic and splanchnic layers.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The splanchnic layer is one of the two unsegmented layers lateral plate mesoderm splits into, not a segmenting tissue itself.
explanations.E: Incorrect. "Branchial" is not a recognised subdivision of intraembryonic mesoderm in this scheme.

questions.learning_objective: State that paraxial mesoderm, unlike intermediate or lateral plate mesoderm, shows segmentation (somite formation).

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table p.19 row 80 (a, remark: "Segmentation is observed in paraxial mesoderm."), confirmed by 600dpi render of p.12 and p.19

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Sources of intraembryonic mesoderm (all-of-above)
questions.question: Sources of intraembryonic mesoderm:

explanations.A: Incorrect on its own. The primitive streak is a genuine source, but not the only one.
explanations.B: Incorrect on its own. The primitive node is a genuine source, but not the only one.
explanations.C: Incorrect on its own. The notochord is a genuine source, but not the only one.
explanations.D: Correct. Epiblast cells ingress not only through the primitive streak but also through the primitive node and give rise to the notochord, so all three, the primitive streak itself, the primitive node, and the notochord, contribute intraembryonic mesoderm. Because the question lists all three genuine sources as separate options, the combined "all of the above" answer is the only complete one.
explanations.E: Incorrect, since option D correctly names all three sources.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Sites where intraembryonic mesoderm is absent (all-of-above)
questions.question: Intraembryonic mesoderm is absent in:

explanations.A: Incorrect on its own. The notochord occupies the median strip between ectoderm and endoderm that intraembryonic mesoderm does not otherwise fill, so this is one genuine absence-adjacent site, but not the only one.
explanations.B: Incorrect on its own. The oropharyngeal (bucco-pharyngeal) membrane is a genuine site where ectoderm and endoderm fuse directly with no mesoderm between them, but not the only one.
explanations.C: Incorrect on its own. The prochordal plate is the small area of tightly adherent ectoderm-endoderm that becomes the oropharyngeal membrane, a genuine absence-adjacent site, but not the only one.
explanations.D: Incorrect on its own. The cloacal membrane is the other genuine site where ectoderm and endoderm fuse directly, but not the only one.
explanations.E: Correct. The notochord and neural tube occupy a median strip between ectoderm and endoderm that intraembryonic mesoderm does not otherwise fill. The prochordal plate/oropharyngeal membrane at the cranial end and the cloacal membrane at the caudal end are the other two sites of direct ectoderm-endoderm fusion. Taken together these are the full set of places where intraembryonic mesoderm is absent, so "all of the above" is the complete answer.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Origin of the neural plate
questions.question: Neural plate is derived from:

options.E: Ectoderm on whole dorsal aspect of embryo

explanations.A: Incorrect. The notochord induces the neural plate to form, but the plate itself is not derived from the notochord.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mesoderm lies beneath the notochord and forms the somites and other mesodermal structures, not the neural plate.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Endoderm forms the gut tube lining, unrelated to the neural plate.
explanations.D: Correct. The notochord induces the ectoderm lying directly above (dorsal to) it to thicken. This thickened strip is the neural plate, a specific, notochord-overlying region of ectoderm rather than the whole dorsal ectodermal surface. The neural plate then sinks as a groove whose lips, the neural folds, meet and fuse to form the neural tube.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Only the ectoderm dorsal to the notochord specifically, not the whole dorsal aspect of the embryo, thickens into the neural plate; the ectoderm lateral to this region remains surface (epidermal) ectoderm.

questions.title: Site where ectoderm and endoderm meet at the cranial end of the notochord
questions.question: At the cranial end of the notochord, ectoderm & endoderm meet at:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The primitive node lies at the streak's cranial end but is not itself a site of direct ectoderm-endoderm fusion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The cloacal membrane is the equivalent fusion site at the caudal, not cranial, end of the embryo.
explanations.C: Correct. Beyond the notochord's cranial end lies the prochordal plate, a small area of tightly adherent ectoderm and endoderm with no intervening mesoderm. This area becomes the oropharyngeal (bucco-pharyngeal) membrane, the future site of the oral opening. It is the cranial counterpart of the cloacal membrane at the embryo's caudal end.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heart-forming (cardiogenic) mesoderm lies in the region that will become ventral to the developing heart, not at a site of direct ectoderm-endoderm fusion.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The neural plate is ectoderm thickened by notochord induction, not a site of ectoderm-endoderm fusion.

questions.subject: dev

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: True statement about the notochord
questions.question: The notochord:

options.A: Is derived from roof of yolk sac
options.B: Forms the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral disc
options.C: Is found caudal to cloacal membrane

explanations.A: Incorrect. The notochord is derived from epiblast cells that ingress through the primitive pit and node, not from the roof of the yolk sac (though its transient notochordal plate stage briefly lies within that roof before folding into the definitive notochord).
explanations.B: Correct. Most of the notochord degenerates as the sclerotome-derived vertebral bodies form around it. The portion lying within each intervertebral disc, between adjacent vertebral bodies, escapes this degeneration. It instead persists as the nucleus pulposus, the gel-like core of the disc.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The notochord extends cranially from the primitive node to the prochordal plate, well cranial to the cloacal membrane at the embryo's caudal end.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The notochord induces the overlying ectoderm to form the neural plate and, in turn, the spinal cord, but the notochord itself does not form the spinal cord.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The sclerotome cells of the somites, not the notochord itself, form the bodies of the vertebrae, migrating to surround the notochord.

questions.question: Definitive yolk sac:

options.B: Has a wall made of ectoderm
options.D: May be found in amniotic cavity

explanations.A: Incorrect. The definitive (secondary) yolk sac's cavity is lined by endoderm, not mesoderm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The definitive yolk sac's wall is endodermal, not ectodermal.
explanations.C: Correct. As folding proceeds and the gut tube closes off, the secondary yolk sac becomes compressed into the narrow vitelline duct. explanations.D: Incorrect. The definitive yolk sac's remnant lies within the umbilical cord, not free within the amniotic cavity.

questions.question: Secondary yolk sac cavity is lined by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ectoderm does not line the secondary yolk sac cavity.

This endodermal lining persists even after the sac is compressed into the vitelline duct.
explanations.D: Incorrect, since only endoderm, not all three germ layers, lines the cavity.

questions.title: False statement about the amnion

options.B: It acts as a protective water jacket for the body
options.D: It is a medium for excretion of urine
options.E: It forms the bag of forewater during labor

explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). The fluid-filled amnion cushions and protects the fetus like a water jacket.
explanations.C: Correct. This is the false statement, the one the question asks for. The amnion's fluid-filled cavity permits, rather than prevents, fetal movement, since it gives the fetus room to move that a closely apposed membrane would not.

explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). The amnion, with the chorion, forms the bag of forewaters that ruptures ahead of delivery.

questions.title: False statement -- structure NOT normally in the primitive umbilical cord
questions.question: The primitive umbilical cord contains all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this IS present in the primitive cord). The vitelline duct connects the midgut to the secondary yolk sac through the primitive cord.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this IS present, though phrased loosely). A pair of umbilical veins is present primitively (the right one degenerates only later), so "one umbilical vein" among the pair is a true, if incomplete, statement.

explanations.D: Correct. This is the false statement, the one the question asks for. The primitive umbilical cord contains a pair of umbilical arteries, not just one; it is only later, at full term, that the cord's vessel complement has narrowed to two arteries and one vein (the right umbilical vein having degenerated), so "one umbilical artery" understates the primitive cord's actual vessel count.
explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. this IS present in the primitive cord). Extraembryonic coelom persists within the primitive cord until it is obliterated later in gestation.

questions.title: False statement about umbilical cord anomalies
questions.question: As regards anomalies of umbilical cord, the following are true EXCEPT:

options.A: A long cord may coil around the neck of the fetus
options.B: A short cord may cause early placental separation
options.C: A true knot is due to local accumulation of Wharton's jelly
options.D: A false knot does not affect the fetus
options.E: In battledore placenta, the umbilical cord is attached to margin of placenta

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). An excessively long cord may coil around the fetal neck (nuchal cord).
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this IS true). An excessively short cord can cause premature (early) placental separation as the fetus descends.
explanations.C: Correct. This is the false statement, the one the question asks for, as worded in this source. A genuine cord knot forms from actual looping of the cord around itself; local accumulation of Wharton's jelly instead produces a false knot, a harmless local swelling with no true looping, so attributing a true knot to Wharton's jelly accumulation reverses the standard true/false knot distinction.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: Period of pregnancy with the greatest teratogenic risk
questions.question: Drugs will produce the greater teratogenic effect during the following period of pregnancy:

options.B: During the first 10-12 weeks of pregnancy
options.E: At the terminal stage of pregnancy

explanations.A: Incorrect. Exposure right at the day of conception, during the pre-embryonic period, classically produces an all-or-none response (death of the conceptus or no lasting effect) rather than the major structural malformations the term "teratogenic" usually implies.
explanations.B: Correct. The first 10-12 weeks of pregnancy correspond to the embryonic period, the window of organogenesis. The developing organ systems are laying down their basic structure during exactly this window, making them most sensitive to disruption. Teratogen exposure during this window therefore carries the greatest risk of major congenital malformations.
explanations.C: Incorrect. By 20-25 weeks, most organ systems have already completed their major structural development, so exposure at this stage more often affects growth or function rather than causing the major malformations typical of first-trimester exposure.
explanations.D: Incorrect. By 25-30 weeks, organogenesis is essentially complete; teratogenic risk at this stage is lower than during the embryonic period.
explanations.E: Incorrect. At the terminal (late third-trimester) stage, organs are fully formed, so exposure at this stage carries the least risk of the major structural malformations that define classic teratogenic effects.

questions.learning_objective: State that teratogenic risk for major structural malformation is greatest during the first 10-12 weeks of pregnancy, the embryonic period/organogenesis window.

explanations.B: Incorrect. Smooth muscle of the esophageal wall is formed by the splanchnic, not somatic, layer of lateral plate mesoderm, since it lines the gut tube.
explanations.C: Correct. The somatic (parietal) layer of lateral plate mesoderm stays applied to the overlying ectoderm as the coelom forms between the two lateral plate layers. The somatic layer specifically contributes the body wall's supportive connective-tissue elements, alongside the parietal layer of each serous membrane.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The muscles of the trunk (myotomes) come from paraxial mesoderm (the somites), not lateral plate mesoderm.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The dermis of the skin comes from the dermatome portion of the somites (paraxial mesoderm), not the somatic layer of lateral plate mesoderm.

questions.subject: dev
questions.title: True statement about the allantois
questions.question: As regards the allantois, choose the correct statement:

options.A: Is a diverticulum of the hindgut
options.C: Is an outpouching of the coelom into the connecting stalk
options.D: Is not found in the umbilical cord at any time

explanations.A: Correct. The allantois arises early in development as a small, finger-like diverticulum (outpouching) from the caudal wall of the yolk sac. It forms in continuity with the hindgut, which is why it is described as a diverticulum of the hindgut. From there, it extends into the connecting stalk that will become the umbilical cord.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The allantois does not completely degenerate; in humans, its remnant persists postnatally as the urachus, a fibrous cord running from the bladder to the umbilicus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The allantois is a diverticulum of the hindgut/yolk sac, not an outpouching of the coelom.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The allantois is found within the umbilical cord from early development onward, since it projects into the connecting stalk that becomes the cord.
explanations.E: Incorrect, since only option A is correct.

questions.question: All the following are mesodermal derivatives EXCEPT:

explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this IS mesodermal). The kidneys develop from intermediate mesoderm.

questions.title: True statement about the somites (all-of-above)
questions.question: As regards the somites, choose the correct statement:

options.A: Differentiate into myotomes which give rise to muscles of trunk
options.B: Differentiate into sclerotomes which give rise to vertebrae
options.C: Arise by segmentation of paraxial mesoderm
options.D: Differentiate into dermatomes which give rise to dermis of skin

explanations.A: Incorrect on its own. This is a genuine fact about somites, but not the only one.
explanations.B: Incorrect on its own. This is a genuine fact about somites, but not the only one.
explanations.C: Incorrect on its own. This is a genuine fact about somites, but not the only one.
explanations.D: Incorrect on its own. This is a genuine fact about somites, but not the only one.
explanations.E: Correct. Somites arise by segmentation of paraxial mesoderm. Each somite then splits into a myotome, giving the muscles of the trunk, a sclerotome, giving the vertebrae, and a dermatome, giving the dermis of the skin. All four listed statements are therefore simultaneously true, making "all of the above" the complete answer.
